name: Land and Power: Critical Perspectives on Belonging and Dispossession
description: Understanding land; indigenous versus western ontologies of land; theorizing land: Marxist, structuralist, phenomenological, post-structural, and postcolonial thoughts; critiques of the dominant conception of land in development discourses; technologies of control: survey, map, and census; restructuring agrarian life through tenure systems; forests, nomads, and the criminalization of non-sedentary life; construction of ‘wasteland’; land governance through knowledge regimes; counter-knowledges; land and belonging: caste, class, race, gender, indigeneity; developmental state and the reproduction of dispossession; agrarian change and the agrarian question; urban land, infrastructure, and informality; land and ecology; historical and contemporary movements for land redistribution, recognition, restoration, and reclamation; anti-dispossession and anti-eviction movements.
